text:
I would like on this divine October afternoon

to stroll along the far shore of the sea;

for the golden sand, and the green waters,

and the pure skies to see me pass.


I would like to be tall, proud, perfect,

like a Roman woman, to accord

with the great waves, and the dead rocks

and the wide beaches that gird the sea.


With slow step, and cold eyes

and mute mouth, let myself be carried;

see how the blue waves break

against the granites and not blink;

see how birds of prey eat

the little fish and not wake;

think that the fragile boats could

sink in the waters and not sigh;

see that the most beautiful man advances,

throat to the air, and not desire to love...


Lose my gaze, distractedly,

lose it and never find it again:

and, erect figure, between sky and beach,

feel myself the perennial oblivion of the sea.

translation.title: Pain
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the wish for cold, statuesque detachment beside the sea.
